groups.title: System Design and Coordination
groups.label: Design & Coordination
groups.blurb: From components to working systems: composition, resources, workloads.

questions.label: q:composition
questions.text: How should RAG operations be composed into a complete workflow?

questions.label: q:coupling
questions.text: At which stages and through which interfaces should external knowledge enter the system?

questions.label: q:scheduling
questions.text: How should retrieval and generation be scheduled within and across requests under a shared resource budget?

questions.label: q:configuration
questions.text: Which system configuration best satisfies the task objectives and resource constraints?

questions.label: q:coordination
questions.text: Which components should change, and how should their updates be coordinated?

questions.label: q:feedback
questions.text: How can downstream outcomes provide useful feedback to upstream decisions?

questions.label: q:conditions
questions.text: Which design and optimization choices must change under different knowledge and deployment conditions?
questions.section: Cross-Cutting System Variants and Deployment Settings

groups.title: Agentic RAG: Runtime Control, Memory, and Collaboration
groups.label: Runtime Control
groups.blurb: When the coordination itself becomes adaptive: search, memory, multi-agent work.

questions.label: q:agency
questions.text: Which retrieval-related decisions are delegated, and what state makes them revisable?

questions.label: q:agent-plan
questions.text: How should a controller plan evidence acquisition when subgoals and source capabilities are uncertain?

questions.label: q:agent-revise
questions.text: How should new observations revise the evidence state and subsequent retrieval actions?

questions.label: q:agent-stop
questions.text: When should search continue, change strategy, abstain, or terminate?

questions.label: q:agent-memory-role
questions.text: What information should persist, for which decisions, and over what lifetime?

questions.label: q:agent-memory-update
questions.text: How should memory be written, retrieved, revised, and forgotten as evidence changes?

questions.label: q:agent-memory-use
questions.text: How can memory improve current decisions without importing stale, unsupported, or unauthorized assumptions?

questions.label: q:agent-delegate
questions.text: When should retrieval-related work be delegated, and how should roles be specialized?

questions.label: q:agent-communicate
questions.text: What should agents exchange, and how should evidence and task state remain consistent?

questions.label: q:agent-reconcile
questions.text: How should a team resolve disagreement and assign responsibility for its final claims?

questions.label: q:agent-interface
questions.text: Which actions and observations should the runtime expose, and within which authority boundaries?

questions.label: q:agent-execution
questions.text: How should the runtime make state transitions, retries, and recovery bounded and auditable?

questions.label: q:agent-observe
questions.text: What must be monitored to establish reliable, resource-bounded execution?

questions.label: q:agent-learn-object
questions.text: Which stateful decisions should training improve, and over what horizon?

questions.label: q:agent-learn-feedback
questions.text: How can trajectory feedback teach useful decisions without rewarding shortcuts or leaking privileged information?

questions.label: q:agent-transfer
questions.text: What learned behavior transfers when tools, evidence, and resource budgets change?

questions.label: q:agent-compare
questions.text: Which matched comparisons substantiate a claimed agentic capability?
questions.section: Comparative Analysis of Agentic RAG Methods

groups.title: Evaluation of RAG: Objects, Quality Dimensions, Settings, and Methods
groups.label: Evaluation
groups.blurb: What an evaluation claim actually establishes, from source defects to end-to-end success.

questions.label: q:eval-claim
questions.text: What precisely is the evaluation claim, and which observations could support it?

questions.label: q:eval-source
questions.text: Does the available knowledge support the task, and which source defects limit the attainable answer?

questions.label: q:eval-retrieval
questions.text: How well does retrieval rank useful evidence and assemble a jointly sufficient set?

questions.label: q:eval-context
questions.text: Was sufficient evidence preserved in the context, and did the generator use it appropriately?

questions.label: q:eval-response
questions.text: Which claims does the response make, and are they correct, supported, and appropriately attributed?

questions.label: q:eval-system
questions.text: What does end-to-end task success reveal, and which failures remain hidden?

questions.label: q:eval-trajectory
questions.text: Which states, actions, and interactions must be observed to evaluate a stateful RAG system?

questions.label: q:eval-quality
questions.text: How should correctness, request relevance, and information coverage be measured without conflating them?

questions.label: q:eval-support
questions.text: What exactly does a grounding or attribution score establish about evidence and the answer?

questions.label: q:eval-robustness
questions.text: Which changes should preserve an answer, and which should cause it to change?

questions.label: q:eval-risk
questions.text: Which harms or disparities are tested, at what boundary, and against which threat or population model?

questions.label: q:eval-cost
questions.text: What task quality and useful throughput are sustained under specified latency, cost, and load constraints?

questions.label: q:eval-domain
questions.text: Which domain conditions and source assumptions make an evaluation representative of its intended use?

questions.label: q:eval-language
questions.text: How should language and cultural coverage be separated from retrieval, generation, and judge performance?

questions.label: q:eval-modality
questions.text: At what evidence granularity should multimodal retrieval, reasoning, and attribution be assessed?

questions.label: q:eval-interaction
questions.text: How should dialogue history, user interaction, and answer form enter the evaluation unit?

questions.label: q:eval-dynamics
questions.text: How should changing knowledge and controlled stressors be introduced without changing the claim unnoticed?

questions.label: q:eval-metric
questions.text: Which reference-based or executable metric validly measures the intended property?

questions.label: q:eval-judge
questions.text: How should a learned evaluator be validated for the decisions its scores will support?

questions.label: q:eval-human
questions.text: Which human judgments are needed, and how should annotation and automated assessment be combined?

questions.label: q:eval-intervention
questions.text: Which interventions can identify evidence use or component contribution, and under which assumptions?

questions.label: q:eval-online
questions.text: How should continuing evaluation separate system improvement from changes in users, sources, and judges?

questions.label: q:eval-benchmark
questions.text: Which combination of benchmarks and infrastructure can support the intended evaluation claims?

questions.label: q:eval-agent-search
questions.text: How can evaluation distinguish useful planning, revision, and stopping from merely longer search?

questions.label: q:eval-agent-memory
questions.text: What controlled evidence establishes the contribution of memory and multi-agent collaboration?

questions.label: q:eval-reported
questions.text: Which conclusions can the reported common-protocol results support, and which remain unidentifiable?
questions.section: Reassessing Reported Results for RL-Trained RAG Systems

questions.label: q:eval-report
questions.text: Which uncertainty, versioning, and reporting practices make a comparative claim reproducible and appropriately limited?

groups.title: Open Challenges and Future Directions
groups.label: Open Frontiers
groups.blurb: The questions the field has not answered yet.

questions.label: q:future-agency
questions.text: Under what workload conditions does observation-conditioned control improve the quality–latency–cost trade-off over prescribed or once-routed workflows?
questions.section: Foundations: Workload-Conditional Control and Composable Quality

questions.label: q:future-contracts
questions.text: Which interface conditions let locally improved components preserve end-to-end evidence validity when they are recombined?
questions.section: Foundations: Workload-Conditional Control and Composable Quality

questions.label: q:future-credit
questions.text: When can long-horizon feedback identify useful retrieval decisions rather than merely reinforce successful-looking trajectories?
questions.section: Learning: Identifiable Credit and Transferable Policies

questions.label: q:future-transfer
questions.text: Can policies learn portable information goals without binding them to a particular retrieval backend or reward judge?
questions.section: Learning: Identifiable Credit and Transferable Policies

questions.label: q:future-stopping
questions.text: How can retrieval and stopping policies preserve required answer quality as evidence availability, service load, and search costs change?

questions.label: q:future-revision
questions.text: How can a source correction or withdrawal propagate through indices, contexts, and derived memories without erasing needed provenance?

questions.label: q:future-memory
questions.text: Can selective persistence remain beneficial over task streams in which both evidence and access permissions change?

questions.label: q:future-collaboration
questions.text: Which task, source, and load conditions justify dynamic team allocation beyond a single controller or fixed team?
questions.section: Conditional Scaling of Multi-Agent and Swarm-Oriented RAG

questions.label: q:future-modal
questions.text: How can cross-modal transformations preserve the evidence units and qualifications needed to verify a generated claim?

questions.label: q:future-domain
questions.text: Which evidence-selection and abstention policies transfer to domains where source authority, time, and access determine answerability?

questions.label: q:future-integrity
questions.text: Can evidence integrity and action boundaries be preserved when retrieved content, source structure, or shared state is adversarial?

questions.label: q:future-privacy
questions.text: How can privacy claims cover repeated retrieval, generation, and memory reuse rather than only one protected interface?

questions.label: q:future-fairness
questions.text: How can disparity be located and reduced across evidence availability, retrieval exposure, and attributed answers without concealing utility losses?

questions.label: q:future-standardization
questions.text: What workload and reporting infrastructure makes RAG quality, efficiency, and scaling evidence comparable without imposing a universal score?

questions.label: q:future-native
questions.text: Which acquisition and reasoning interfaces should be learned jointly, and which should remain explicit to preserve replaceability and audit?
